description: Imports PostHog product-analytics data (organizations, projects, events, persons, cohorts, feature flags, annotations) for every project in one PostHog organization.

baseUrl.resolution: User-supplied endpoint config field `advanced.base_url`, defaulting to https://app.posthog.com. Docs point EU cloud users at https://eu.posthog.com; because PostHog is self-hostable any host may be given. All request URLs are built by urljoin()-ing 'api/...' segments onto this value.

continuity.notes: Pure read-only HTTP polling: no replication slot, consumer group, scratch table, or other server-side object is created in PostHog. All resumption state is datetime cursors held in Flow connector state, so an arbitrarily long pause only means a larger catch-up query on the next tick. The only in-process state is estuary_cdk.emitted_changes_cache, used to suppress duplicate events between the realtime and 1h-lookback event streams; losing it on restart causes re-emission (idempotent on the /_meta/project_id + /uuid key), not data loss.

discovery.method: Fixed 7-resource list, then filtered at discover/validate time by the scopes reported for the personal API key at GET api/personal_api_keys/@current
discovery.querySketch: GET {base_url}/api/personal_api_keys/@current -> {scopes: [...]}; a resource is kept when its required scope is present, or when the key is scoped '*'
discovery.allowlist: Cohorts requires cohort:read, FeatureFlags requires feature_flag:read, Annotations requires annotation:read, Events and Persons require query:read. Organizations and Projects have no scope requirement and are always offered.

pathPlaceholders.project_id: iterated over every project id returned by the Projects stream (GET api/organizations/{organization_id}/projects/)
iterated over every project id returned by the Projects stream
one backfill fetcher is registered per project id
one incremental fetcher is registered per project id

schedules.role: incremental sweep (both the realtime and the 1h-lookback sub-streams)

backfill.querySketch: POST api/projects/{project_id}/query with body {query: {kind: 'HogQLQuery', query: "SELECT <columns discovered via a LIMIT 0 probe> FROM events WHERE COALESCE(timestamp) > toDateTime64(<cursor>,6,'UTC') AND COALESCE(timestamp) <= toDateTime64(<cutoff>,6,'UTC') ORDER BY COALESCE(timestamp) ASC LIMIT 50000"}}; rows come back as positional arrays under results and are zipped with the columns list. Loops, advancing the cursor to the max timestamp seen, until a batch returns fewer than 50000 rows. A 5-minute wall-clock backfill timeout emits a PageCursor at the last fully-consumed timestamp.

incremental.querySketch: Same HogQL POST, lower bound = stored cursor. Two sub-streams per project: '{project_id}_realtime' with no upper bound, and '{project_id}_lookback' with upper bound now-1h to re-read events delayed by ClickHouse/Kafka. Duplicates between the two are suppressed via emitted_changes_cache keyed '{project_id}/{uuid}'.

backfill.querySketch: POST api/projects/{project_id}/query with a HogQLQuery: SELECT <probed columns> FROM persons WHERE COALESCE(last_seen_at,created_at) > toDateTime64(<cursor>,6,'UTC') AND COALESCE(...) <= toDateTime64(<cutoff>,6,'UTC') ORDER BY COALESCE(...) ASC LIMIT 50000, looping until a short batch; wrapped in the same 5-minute backfill timeout.

incremental.querySketch: Same HogQL POST with lower bound = stored cursor and NO upper bound; loops until a batch shorter than 50000 rows.

authTierRationale: Exactly one credential mode. The user pastes a single self-serve PostHog Personal API Key (phx_...) which is sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` by the CDK's TokenSource for the CDK AccessToken credential type. `TokenSource(oauth_spec=None, ...)` is constructed with a null OAuth spec, so no OAuth app registration and no refresh token are involved. The only extra user-supplied values are the organization UUID and, for self-hosted/EU installs, the base URL.

unionMisfits.description: The HogQL streams have no HTTP paginator at all: pagination is keyset pagination expressed inside the SQL text of the POST body. The page token is the max cursor-column value of the last row returned (record_cursor-like), it is sent embedded in a SQL WHERE clause inside a JSON request body (body_cursor-like), and the loop terminates when a batch returns fewer than the LIMIT of 50000 rows (short_page). None of the seven paginator types describes this, so the field is omitted rather than mis-typed and the mechanism is written into querySketch.

One binding fans out into 2 x N concurrent sub-streams (N = number of projects in the org, discovered at runtime), and the two per-project sub-streams differ only in an upper time bound (realtime = unbounded, lookback = now minus 1h) to absorb PostHog's eventual consistency. The schema's single `incremental` PullSpec cannot express per-binding fan-out or two differently-lagged legs of the same leg-type.

Every project-scoped stream is a runtime fan-out over project ids fetched from a parent endpoint, not a single path with a placeholder. pathPlaceholders can name the variable but cannot express that the connector iterates all values and interleaves the resulting documents into one collection distinguished by /_meta/project_id.

streamMode is `static` (a hard-coded list of 7), yet the offered list is narrowed at runtime by the API key's scopes. That is neither pure static nor schema discovery; `discovery` is filled in here to record the scope filter even though `streamMode` is static.

abstained.streams[5].pull.backfill.paginator: The HogQL POST has no HTTP paginator; paging is a SQL keyset loop (LIMIT 50000, cursor advanced to the max value seen, stop on a short batch). Emitting any of the seven paginator types would misdescribe it, so it is recorded in unionMisfits and querySketch instead.
abstained.streams[5].pull.incremental.paginator: Same as backfill: SQL keyset loop inside the request body, not an HTTP paginator.
abstained.streams[4].pull.incremental.incrementalP: No server-side time filter is sent. The connector relies solely on ?order=-updated_at and breaks out of the result stream client-side once it sees a record at or below the stored cursor; there is no since/updated_after query parameter in the code.
abstained.streams[*].pull.snapshot.params (order f: Organizations and Projects use their own URL builders which do NOT append ?order=-updated_at; only the ProjectEntity builder (Cohorts, Annotations, FeatureFlags) appends it.
abstained.transports[0].spec.apiVersionPinning: No version header, path segment, or query parameter appears anywhere; the connector hits unversioned /api/ paths.
abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders: Only the Authorization header injected by the CDK's HTTPSession is set; no connector-specific default headers were found.
abstained.streams[*].pull.*.pageSize (REST): No page-size or limit parameter is sent on any REST endpoint; PostHog's server-side default is accepted and the `next` URL is followed verbatim.
abstained.execution.continuity.resumeWindow: Nothing in the connector bounds how long it may pause. PostHog's own event/ClickHouse retention could in principle age out data older than the stored cursor, but no retention assumption is encoded in the code, so no window is asserted.
